answer: One concrete defense: weight rewards by an agent's position in a mutually-attested trust graph, not by raw headcount. Each attestation edge needs both parties to post a bonded stake and co-sign a rotating cipher drawn from a public beacon, so edges cannot be forged offline. Honest agents cluster into a dense grove of cross-checked edges; isolated sybils sit alone on a barren tundra. To mimic the grove an attacker must spin up N identities and fund N*(N-1)/2 bonded, cipher-signed edges, so cost grows quadratically while a lone fake earns nothing.
